```{r}

prediet <- c(140,160,135,120,125,165,108,130,225,140,180)

postdiet <- c(139,155,120,118,123,155,108,129,195,142,176)

weight_loss <- prediet - postdiet

print(weight_loss[5])

fifth_weigh_loss_value <- weight_loss[5]/2.2

print(class(fifth_weigh_loss_value))
weight_loss_kg <- weight_loss / 2.2

data <- data.frame(prediet,postdiet, weight_loss, weight_loss_kg)
print(mean(data$weight_loss_kg))
print(median(data$weight_loss_kg))
print(min(data$weight_loss_kg))
print(max(data$weight_loss_kg))
summary(data$weight_loss_kg)

data$weight_gain_category <- ifelse(data$weight_loss > 0, "loss", "gain")
is.character(data$weight_gain_category)

t.test(x = prediet, y = postdiet, paired = TRUE)

t.test(x=weight_loss)


```

## Inference

$H_0: \mu_{diff} = 0$

$H_A: \mu_{diff} \neq 0$

$\alpha = 0.01$

Fail to reject $H_0$ - we do not have sufficient evidence to claim that the diet/program was
effective.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
patients <- read_csv("data/patients.csv",na = c("Not recorded",".")) # this specifies what else can be interpreted as NA.
glimpse(patients)


write_csv(patients, "data/patients_clean.csv")

patient_clean <- read_csv("data/patients_clean.csv")
glimpse(patient_clean)
```

### Typical data-analysis workflow

1. Import the data
2. Inspect its structure and contents
3. Identify the relevant question and variables
4. Clean the data as necessary
5. Visualize and analyze the data
6. Communicate what you learn
